title: Insider-transaction cluster callouts — non-blocking review follow-ups
description: Non-blocking finding from pr-reviewer's full review of PR #195 (frontend-insider-clusters-badge), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so it isn't lost once that PR merges.

checklist.step: The most-recent-window_end_date-first sort comparator (`a.window_end_date < b.window_end_date ? 1 : -1`) is duplicated verbatim between FundamentalDataPanel.tsx's InsiderClusterCallouts (line ~113) and metricHelpContent.ts's insiderClustersHelp.interpretValue (line ~1167) instead of sharing one implementation. Not a correctness bug today, but a maintenance hazard: if the comparator is ever corrected (e.g. a tie-break, or an equal-date edge case) in one copy, it's easy to update only one call site, leaving the callout list and the MetricHelp text silently disagreeing on cluster order for the same ticker. Extract a single shared sort helper (e.g. colocated in metricHelpContent.ts or a small shared util) and have both call sites use it.

decisions.decision: Extracted the comparator into a new frontend/src/utils/insiderClusters.ts (`sortClustersByRecentWindowEnd`), with its own colocated unit test, rather than colocating it inside metricHelpContent.ts as the checklist step's parenthetical suggested.
decisions.rationale: frontend/src/utils/ already holds exactly this shape of small, single-purpose, independently-tested cross-component helper (signColor.ts, format.ts, chart.ts), including a prior instance of this same pattern -- signColor.ts's own doc comment records it was extracted from duplicated inline logic for the same reason. Colocating in metricHelpContent.ts would have made FundamentalDataPanel.tsx import a sort helper from a file whose own module doc describes it as MetricHelp registry content, coupling two unrelated concerns for no benefit.

comments.summary: Verified `sortClustersByRecentWindowEnd` is byte-for-byte behavior-identical to both original inline implementations: FundamentalDataPanel.tsx used `[...clusters].sort((a, b) => a.window_end_date < b.window_end_date ? 1 : -1)`, metricHelpContent.ts used `clusters.slice().sort((a, b) => (a.window_end_date < b.window_end_date ? 1 : -1))` -- `.slice()` with no args and `[...clusters]` are equivalent shallow copies, and the comparator itself is unchanged. No subtle difference slipped in.

New unit tests in insiderClusters.test.ts are meaningfully exercising the sort (three differently-dated clusters asserted into a specific most-recent-first order; a non-mutation check that the input array/objects are untouched and a new array is returned; an empty-array edge case) -- not tautological.

Placement in frontend/src/utils/insiderClusters.ts matches the documented precedent: signColor.ts, format.ts, and chart.ts are all small, single-purpose, independently-tested cross-component helpers in the same directory, and signColor.ts's own doc comment records the identical extract-from-duplicated-inline-logic pattern. The task's decisions entry records this rationale (and why colocating in metricHelpContent.ts, as the original checklist step's parenthetical suggested, was rejected). Satisfies CLAUDE.md's decision-memory requirement.

Pre-existing, not introduced by this PR: the comparator (`a.window_end_date < b.window_end_date ? 1 : -1`) never returns 0 for equal window_end_date values, so ties don't sort transitively/stably. This existed identically in both original call sites before this refactor and is exactly the 'equal-date edge case' the parent task's checklist item already named as deferred, out-of-scope future work ('Not a correctness bug today'). Consolidating it into one shared function is a net improvement (a future fix now only needs to touch one place) rather than a regression, so not treated as a new finding and no new followup task filed per this review's scope.

review.notes: Small, well-scoped refactor-only PR. Backend suite: 920 passed, 99.94% coverage (unaffected, sanity-checked since untouched by this diff). Frontend suite: 684/685 passed under default parallel execution with one flaky timeout in an unrelated pre-existing test (PortfolioPage.test.tsx / MethodologyPage.test.tsx alternately, both userEvent-based tests unrelated to this diff) that reproduces even on a clean checkout of this same branch and disappears entirely when re-run with --no-file-parallelism (685/685 passed, 99.64% statements / 98.94% branches / 99.72% functions / 99.71% lines, all well above the 90% gate) -- confirmed as resource-contention flakiness in this sandbox, not a regression from this change. eslint and tsc -b --noEmit both clean. code-review skill (medium effort) found no correctness, reuse, simplification, or efficiency issues beyond the pre-existing tie-break behavior noted above. Full Playwright e2e suite (make e2e, 16/16 specs) passed cleanly including console-error and stock-analysis-page checks; no interactive Playwright MCP browser tool was available in this session, so the exploratory walkthrough step relied on: the e2e run's own console/network checks, the existing FundamentalDataPanel.test.tsx component test 'shows multiple clusters, most recent window first' (real DOM rendering via Testing Library exercising the exact call site with cluster data), and the new unit tests -- noting explicitly that the e2e fixture data provider has no synthetic insider-transaction data for any fixture ticker (see app/data/fixture_provider.py and stock-analysis.spec.ts's own empty-state assertion), so no persisted or ad hoc browser check can currently exercise live cluster rendering without a real/live data provider; this is a pre-existing gap in the fixture data, not something this PR needed to address. No API/schema change (openapi.json untouched, correctly). No new module/dependency/layer, so architecture-review was not separately invoked -- placement reasoning was checked directly against the cited precedent. Area is frontend/pages/stocks with skill null, not backend/signals or backend/portfolio, so verify-elder-signal does not apply.
